cards.text: Isaiah, the prophet, has just told of that day, when the LORD will take His great sword and bring judgment on Leviathan, the serpent (Isaiah 27:1). Now, in that same day, the LORD Himself calls for a song: "Sing about a fruitful vineyard." Friend, I sat through a LOT of birthday batches in the Millers' kitchen, and not ONCE did anybody sing about me.

cards.question: The LORD calls for a song about a fruitful vineyard. Who does He say is its keeper?

cards.text: And this keeper is HANDS-ON. I set a timer for every single batch and STILL forget, but the LORD says He waters this vineyard continually.

cards.question: The LORD guards His vineyard only during the day.
The LORD guards His vineyard night and day so no one can ___ it.
Right after He talks about guarding His vineyard, the LORD says He is not angry.

cards.text: Then the LORD brings up thorns and briers: "If only thorns and briers confronted Me…"

cards.question: If thorns and briers confronted the LORD, what does He say He would do to them?

answers.text: Trample them and burn them down
Let them grow next to the vines

cards.text: But then comes one little word: "Or". The LORD gives them another option.

cards.question: Right after the thorns and briers, the LORD says to let them lay claim to His protection. What else does He say to let them do?

cards.text: And He says "let them make peace with Me" TWICE.
Then comes a look at the days to come, and two names: Jacob and Israel. Both names point to God's people, who come from Jacob, the forefather God renamed Israel (Genesis 35:10).

cards.question: In the days to come, Israel is pictured like a plant. What happens to it?

answers.text: It takes root and fills the world with fruit
It stays small and hidden in one field
It blooms once but never bears any fruit

cards.text: Now comes a hard question: "Has the LORD struck Israel as He struck her oppressors?" And another one: "Was she killed like those who slayed her?"

cards.question: By warfare and exile, the LORD contended with Israel.

cards.text: The LORD removed her with a fierce wind, as on the day the east wind blows. I think this part is heavy, friend.

cards.question: Therefore Jacob's ___ will be atoned for.
The removal of Jacob's sin will bear full fruit. What will that look like?

answers.text: He makes all the altar stones like crushed chalk
He builds a taller altar of stone
He sets up new carved idols

cards.text: And no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing. That's not wiping a few crumbs off the counter, friend, that's clearing the WHOLE counter.
Then comes the fortified city: deserted, a homestead abandoned, a wilderness forsaken.

cards.question: In the deserted fortified city, calves graze and lie down.

cards.text: The calves strip its branches bare, and when the limbs are dry, women come and use them for kindling. That city went from FORTRESS to FIREWOOD.

cards.question: Their Maker has no compassion on the people there. Why?

answers.text: They are a people without understanding
They live too far from Jerusalem
They lost a long war to Egypt

cards.text: But that's not where it ends. In that day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates River all the way to the Wadi of Egypt.

cards.question: In that day the Israelites are told how they will be gathered. How?

cards.text: One by one, friend, and as a stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer, I LOVE that line. Then, in that day, a sound rings out.

cards.question: In that day a sound rings out. What is it?
When the ram's horn sounds, only those perishing in Assyria come forth, and the exiles in Egypt stay behind.
Those from Assyria and those from Egypt come forth together. Where will they worship the LORD?

answers.text: On the holy mountain in Jerusalem
At the altar in the city of Bethel
In a temple in the land of Egypt
